seoDetails.title: How the formatter works
seoDetails.strictDescription: The tool uses JSON.parse, so JavaScript objects, comments, unquoted keys, and trailing commas are rejected.
seoDetails.minifyDescription: Formatting adds line breaks and indentation for reading. Minification removes unnecessary whitespace and preserves the data.
seoDetails.privacyDescription: Pasted JSON stays in the browser. Include content in the link only when the payload may be read by everyone who receives the URL.

privacy.question: Is the JSON sent to the server?
privacy.answer: No. Parsing, formatting, and minification happen in the browser. Content only enters the link when you enable the include JSON option.

strict.question: Why is JSON with a comment or trailing comma invalid?
strict.answer: Strict JSON does not allow comments, single quotes, unquoted keys, trailing commas, NaN, or Infinity.

difference.question: What is the difference between formatting and minifying JSON?
difference.answer: Formatting adds indentation and line breaks for reading. Minifying removes unnecessary whitespace to reduce payload size.

schema.question: Does this tool validate JSON Schema?
schema.answer: No. It validates JSON syntax only. It does not confirm schemas, API contracts, business rules, or sensitive data.

sharing.question: Can I share prefilled JSON?
sharing.answer: Yes, but only after enabling the option to include JSON in the link. Do not use that with tokens, credentials, personal data, or private payloads.

seo.about: The formatter uses the browser's JSON.parse and JSON.stringify APIs to validate, format, and minify strict JSON. It accepts objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and null, but not relaxed JavaScript syntax.
seo.howToUse: Paste the JSON, choose format, minify, or validate, and check the status. Use copy or download when the result is valid. Shared links preserve only mode and indentation by default.
